Numbering may come from a paragraph style rather than from the paragraph.

1. An item whose style carries the w:numPr.
   1. One whose style inherits the list and names only the level.
2. Back out again.

A numId of 0 cancels what the style supplied.

A List Paragraph with no numbering anywhere is not a list either.

## A numbered heading is a heading

Word's multilevel list linked to headings puts a w:numPr on every heading style.

- > A quotation may be an item of a list as well.
- > And so may the one after it.
- `A monospace item stays an item.`

Row 12's font heuristic is a guess, and a w:numPr is a statement.
